subject: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@finlytics.com>, Aisha Singh <aisha.s@finlytics.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology — post-call recap

Hi Sam / Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and the key items we heard as pain points / objectives:

- Pain points:
  - Tail latency spikes during peak + inconsistent p95 for chat completions (observed spiking to ~600ms).
  - Throughput needs during batch scoring windows (~10-15k records/hour) and sustained live request rates during business hours.
  - Model size & memory footprint constraints in your on-prem environment; need support for quantized weights.
  - Data residency / VPC-only access for sensitive inference workloads.

- Goals / SLOs you mentioned:
  - Interactive chat: target p95 latency <= 250 ms for requests up to 512 tokens.
  - Embeddings / batch scoring: sustained throughput of ~200 requests/sec (amortized during windows), peak bursts to 400/s.
  - Predictable per-token cost and ability to fallback to smaller variants if latency/price spikes.

- Technical constraints:
  - On-prem requirement for production traffic for regulated models; possibility of hybrid approach for non-PII workloads.
  - Current model is a fine-tuned 13B family; willing to consider int8 quantization but need accuracy verification.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Sharing a short SLO + topology proposal (attached: SLO_proposal_v1.xlsx).
2) Schedule a 60m deep-dive next week with your infra and security team to walk deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
3) Red team validation: run a short bench with our recommended config to validate p95 and throughput.

Please confirm availability for the deep-dive (I suggested Tue/Wed next week) and any additional attendees from your infra/security teams. I've cc'd David (solutions architect) to help with the topology sketch.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak concurrency and throughput: our production peak last quarter was ~320 concurrent chat sessions during spike windows; long-term expectation is ~150-200 concurrent. The batch scoring window processes ~12k documents over a 30-60 minute window.
- Model fidelity: we need to maintain current accuracy for named-entity and classification outputs — any quantization must be validated against our holdout prompts.
- Network / residency: we require VPC-only access for the model that processes regulated data; non-regulated workloads can be run in hosted.

I can make Tue (Feb 16) between 09:00-12:00 PT or Wed (Feb 17) after 13:00 PT for the deep-dive. I'll loop our infra lead (Aisha) — she may have additional constraints about outbound peering and egress limits.

Also, would be helpful if you can include a diagram of the recommended deployment topology (VPC setup, NAT/firewall considerations, and whether Dedicated or Private is recommended).

Thanks — Sam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology — recommended config (pre-call)

Hi Sam / team,

Following up with an engineer-first read on the requirements prior to our deep-dive. High-level recommendation based on the target p95 <= 250 ms (<=512 tokens) and sustained throughput goals:

1) Deployment topology:
   - Recommendation: Redwood Private (VPC) deployed in your us-west-2 account using Dedicated capacity pools. This gives VPC-only networking, KMS integration, and predictable capacity for peak windows.
   - Node footprint: start with 4x A100-equivalent instances (single-model-per-node with GPU memory > model size) for the 13B-class model; scale to 6 nodes if throughput testing shows higher batching benefits.
   - Autoscaling: configure policy based on GPU utilization + queue depth to avoid tail-latency spikes during bursts.

2) Model / inference settings:
   - Use quantized int8 variant of your 13B model for production if accuracy checks pass on your holdout. Expect small accuracy deltas (~1-2% on targeted metrics) but large latency/cost gains.
   - Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size 16 for chat; prefer batching window 20-30ms for latency-sensitive paths. For embeddings/batch scoring, use larger batch sizes (64-128) and dedicated batch workers.
   - KV cache & prefix caching: enable prefix KV cache for repeated system prompts to shave p95 by ~30-60ms on typical flows.

3) Network and infra considerations:
   - Egress: ensure NAT throughput and per-node bandwidth meets sustained burst requirements; recommend 10Gbps per GPU node in heavy throughput scenarios.
   - Authentication: KMS for model keys and mTLS between your VPC and Redwood control plane.

4) Bench plan (pre-call action):
   - Redwood will run a synthetic bench mirroring: 512-token average chat requests at 150 concurrent, and embedding batch runs at 200 req/s. We'll share expected p50/p95 p99 and throughput numbers before the call.
   - Finlytics to provide the 10-card holdout prompt set and any acceptance thresholds for accuracy.

Next steps from my side: I'll prepare a short run on the recommended config and upload results + updated SLO sheet prior to Tue 09:30 PT. If you have any hard constraints (e.g., maximum allowed quantization accuracy delta, or strict upper limits on egress) please flag them now so we can incorporate into validation.

Looking forward — Neha
Neha Kapoor
